relevance_note: Single-patient case report of an ABCA1 variant carrier: "a novel heterozygous splicing variant in the ABCA1 gene" in a man with "probable Tangier disease".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short script only assembled the JSON. Proband labelled 'patient' (rule 5; 'our proband' is a role word). Relatives with individual-level data were given rows: youngest brother (HDL-C 35 mg/dL), father (HDL-C 37 mg/dL; died of acute MI in his seventies) and mother (HDL-C 42 mg/dL); none was genetically tested, so they have no variant rows. The 'other four siblings' who declined testing have no individual-level facts and get no rows. Parents' HDL-C described only jointly as 'low to low-normal', so low HDL left not reported for them. Only one ABCA1 variant is printed; the authors state 'The other mutation on ABCA1 has yet to be identified', so no second variant row was created. Table 1 (historical lipid profiles over time, columns are dates, not patients) was used only as context; no checklist status was taken from its numbers. Individual-level age at onset left not reported: ischemic heart disease at 40 years is recorded as a feature onset instead; age at last evaluation not reported (age 50 is stated only at the 2012 admission; follow-up continued to 2023 without an age). Normal findings recorded as excluded abnormalities under D-27: 'normal sensation and reflexes' -> abnormal sensation / abnormal reflexes excluded, but checklist 'reduced tendon reflexes' and 'reduced deep sensation' left not reported as more specific; normal lower-limb nerve conduction -> abnormal nerve conduction excluded, checklist 'peripheral neuropathy' left not reported. 'tonsils were not enlarged' does not exclude the composite checklist item 'orange-colored or enlarged tonsils' (colour not addressed). 'severe hypertriglyceridemia' excluded as a secondary cause; this narrower absence does not exclude checklist 'hypertriglyceridemia'. Low LDL cholesterol marked observed from 'LDL-C of 35 mg/dL ... only'; the paper does not use the word 'low' for this patient. Colonic lipid deposits are described as 'suggestive of fatty deposits' and elsewhere as 'evidence of fatty deposits'; recorded observed. Small dense LDL was only 'suggested' and was not recorded. No contradictions found.
